adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Debug tracing left at r.log.Error (also 537/554/557/576/579) runs on every batch even when nothing is deleted, so each instance logs 2-14 error lines a minute with the 1m ticker, dumps up to batch-size ID arrays (32767 IDs is a ~250KB line), and trips error-log alerting.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — Only SQLite falls back to inlined IDs, so on Postgres/MySQL a cleanupjob_batchsize above 65535 with a backlog that large fails every run with a too-many-placeholders error; cleanup then stops for good and the annotation table grows without bound, which the old single-statement DELETE did not do.

adjudication.rationale: The new cleanup path fetches up to r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize IDs into memory (fetchIDs uses dialect Limit/LimitOffset with that batch size) and then issues `DELETE ... WHERE id IN (?, ?, ...)` with one placeholder per ID in deleteByIDs for all DBs except SQLite. There is no cap/guard for Postgres/MySQL placeholder/parameter limits, so a sufficiently large configured batch size (and enough backlog to fill it) will generate a statement with too many placeholders and fail every run. The prior single-statement DELETE did not create one parameter per row ID, so this failure mode is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Ticker cut from 10m to 1m reruns all eight cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, etc.) 10x as often on every HA instance with no server lock, and with the 9m timeout a slow run is followed right away by the next, so the DB sees constant concurrent cleanup load.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:556 — MaxCount is no longer atomic: the IDs fetched with OFFSET are deleted in a separate statement, so a newer annotation removed between fetch and delete (user delete or another instance) makes this delete rows that are now inside the keep-N window, leaving fewer than MaxCount.

adjudication.rationale: In the MaxCount path, the code now does a separate `SELECT id ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ... OFFSET cfg.MaxCount` via `fetchIDs(...)` and then a second statement `DELETE FROM annotation WHERE id IN (...)` via `deleteByIDs(...)`. Because these are not atomic, if newer annotations (within the keep-`MaxCount` window) are deleted by another actor between the fetch and delete, some IDs that were previously “beyond the offset” can become part of the newest `MaxCount` set before the delete runs, yet they will still be deleted, leaving fewer than `MaxCount` rows even when enough existed at fetch time. This race is enabled by the two-step approach introduced in the diff (previously a single DELETE with subquery/offset).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:611 — The SQLite inline-ID path builds the IN list with repeated fmt.Sprintf, which is O(n^2) in the batch size (about 3-4GB of copying and garbage per 32767-ID batch).

adjudication.rationale: In xorm_store.go `deleteByIDs`, the SQLite fallback builds `values` via `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop over `ids[1:]`. This repeatedly reallocates and copies the growing string, making construction O(n^2) in the number of IDs. With the new test case using a 32767 batch size, this can become a significant performance/memory issue, though it does not change correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:83 — Each subtest now reseeds fresh data, so the "running the max count delete again" case never actually reruns cleanup on already-cleaned state and the idempotence check passes without testing anything.

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, each `t.Run` now calls `createTestAnnotations(...)` and only invokes `cleaner.Run(...)` once, with a per-subtest `t.Cleanup` that clears tables afterward. Therefore the subtest named "running the max count delete again..." no longer runs cleanup on an already-cleaned database state. With the fresh seed for that case (`createAnnotationsNum: 9`, `MaxCount: 3`), the first cleanup should delete 6 annotations, yet the test expects `affectedAnnotations: 0`, so the idempotence scenario is not actually exercised and the expectations appear inconsistent with the new setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — The non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID, so on MySQL and Postgres a configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above 65535 exceeds the driver's placeholder limit and every cleanup fails, which the old subquery DELETE did not do

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteByIDs`, the non-SQLite branch builds an `IN` clause with one `?` placeholder per ID (`placeholders := "?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)`), and `ids` is fetched in a batch sized by `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` (`fetchIDs` uses `Limit(r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize)`). There is no guard for large batch sizes on MySQL/Postgres, so configuring `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` very large can generate a statement with tens of thousands of bound parameters and potentially exceed DB/driver parameter limits, causing cleanup to fail. The previous implementation used a single DELETE with subquery/limit and did not create one bound parameter per row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:97 — The "running the max count delete again" case now seeds fresh data per subtest, so it no longer tests re-running cleanup on already-trimmed data as its name claims

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, each subtest now calls `createTestAnnotations(...)` at the start and registers a per-subtest `t.Cleanup` that deletes `annotation`/`annotation_tag`. Therefore the case named "running the max count delete again should not remove any annotations" no longer re-runs cleanup on already-trimmed data from the prior "should only keep three annotations" case; it runs on a freshly seeded DB and only invokes `cleaner.Run(...)` once.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:118 — t.Cleanup is registered after createTestAnnotations and its require-based count assertions, so a failure during seeding leaves rows in the shared DB and cascades failures into later subtests

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, `fakeSQL := db.InitTestDB(t)` is created once and reused across all `t.Run` subtests. Inside each subtest, `createTestAnnotations(...)` and the subsequent `assertAnnotationCount` / `assertAnnotationTagCount` run *before* the `t.Cleanup(...)` is registered. If seeding or these assertions fail (e.g., via `require.*` inside `createTestAnnotations`), the cleanup is never registered, leaving rows in `annotation`/`annotation_tag` in the shared DB and potentially causing later subtests to fail due to unexpected counts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds three `untilDoneOrCancelled` callbacks in `CleanAnnotations` (MaxAge branch and MaxCount branch) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` that all do the same sequence: build `cond`, call `r.fetchIDs(...)`, log, call `r.deleteByIDs(...)`, log, return affected/error. adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:584 — fetchIDs takes a `condition` parameter that it appends after WHERE, but callers also pass ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET clauses in it, so the name is misleading and the API is a raw-SQL-fragment leak.

adjudication.rationale: In xorm_store.go, fetchIDs builds SQL as `SELECT id FROM %s WHERE %s` and requires `condition` to be non-empty. Callers pass strings like `... ORDER BY id DESC %s` and `... LimitOffset(...)` (e.g., in CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags), meaning `condition` is not just a WHERE predicate but a full tail fragment (predicate + ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET). This is not a correctness defect (the resulting SQL is valid), but it does make the API misleadingly named and leaks raw SQL-fragment construction into callers, increasing maintenance/abstraction risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — The logged "err" field is always nil because the error was already checked and returned just above (same at 554, 576).

adjudication.rationale: In the new cleanup loops, the code logs `"err", err` immediately after `if err != nil { return 0, err }`, so `err` is necessarily nil at those log sites (e.g., after `ids, err := r.fetchIDs(...)` in `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`). This doesn’t break behavior, but it makes the log field misleading/useless (the error would have already short-circuited).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:606 — The comment and the 999 constant describe the pre-3.32 SQLite limit, but the new test (cleanup_test.go:98) cites the >=3.32.0 limit of 32766, so the two disagree about which limit the code handles.

adjudication.rationale: In xorm_store.go, deleteByIDs defines `const sqliteParameterLimit = 999` with the comment "SQLite has a parameter limit of 999" and uses it as the threshold to inline IDs into the SQL when `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit`. The new integration test case is explicitly about SQLite >= 3.32.0 having a much higher SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER (name references 32766/32767). The code will still work (it inlines IDs, avoiding the parameter limit), but the comment/constant rationale is inconsistent with the test’s stated SQLite limit, making the documentation misleading and the threshold potentially outdated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:609 — Inlined ID list is built by repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation (quadratic) instead of strings.Join/strings.Builder, and the SQLite branch is keyed on the configured batch size rather than len(ids).

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteByIDs`, the SQLite path builds the `IN (...)` list by repeatedly reformatting and re-copying the growing string (`values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop), which is a real diff-grounded performance concern for large batches (the test adds a 32k batch). However, the claim that the SQLite branch should key off `len(ids)` rather than the configured batch size isn’t supported by the diff: all callers shown fetch IDs with `Limit(r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize)`, so `len(ids)` is bounded by the configured batch size, making the current condition effectively equivalent in this code path.

This is quadratic-time string concatenation (repeatedly copying the growing string) and is triggered when `r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite` and `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`—which the updated test explicitly exercises with `annotationCleanupJobBatchSize: 32767`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/scalability issue, but it does not by itself demonstrate a correctness failure from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:83 — "running the max count delete again" now seeds a fresh 9-row dataset (3 per type) so nothing exceeds MaxCount=3; it no longer re-runs cleanup on already-cleaned state, so idempotence is untested and the name is misleading

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:523 — The stated motivation (MySQL deadlock with concurrent inserts) has no test; nothing runs cleanup concurrently with inserts, so the fetch-IDs-then-delete rewrite is only checked for count correctness, not for the deadlock fix

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:101 — Only batch sizes 1 and 32767 are tested, so the 999/1000 threshold in deleteByIDs and the SQLite placeholder path with more than one ID per batch are never exercised

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:103 — The large-batch case covers only MaxCount; the MaxAge fetch/delete loop runs only with batch size 1, so MaxAge with multi-ID batches and the SQLite inlined-ID path is untested

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:99 — Each annotation delete in the 40003 case is at most ~13334 IDs, under SQLite's 32766 limit, so only the orphan-tag batch (32767 IDs, one over the limit) would catch a regression in the inlining branch; the coverage is fragile and depends on the build's variable limit

adjudication.rationale: In the added integration case `createAnnotationsNum: 40003` with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize: 32767`, the cleanup code now fetches IDs then calls `deleteByIDs` (SQLite special-casing) in batches. adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:120 — t.Cleanup is registered after createTestAnnotations and the require-based count asserts, so a failure there leaves rows behind and later subtests hit primary-key conflicts on the explicit IDs 1..N, causing cascading failures

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, the subtest registers `t.Cleanup` only after `createTestAnnotations(...)` and the initial `assertAnnotationCount` / `assertAnnotationTagCount` calls. If any of those `require`/`assert` checks fail (or `createTestAnnotations` fails during inserts), the cleanup won’t be registered, leaving rows in `annotation`/`annotation_tag`. Since `createTestAnnotations` now assigns explicit IDs starting at 1 (`ID: int64(i + 1)`), later subtests using the same `fakeSQL` instance (created once before the loop) can hit primary-key conflicts and cascade failures.
